_comment: Example for a Debian server with Docker apps on 127.0.0.1, behind tailscale serve, plus a gaming PC that sleeps. Keys that start with _ are comments. All keys: docs/REFERENCE_SERVER.md.
name: homeserver
_auth: tailscale serve adds Tailscale-User-Login. Only logins listed here get in. Tokens (for tagged devices or curl) come from the env var HOMELAB_TOKENS, so this file holds no secrets.
_allowed_hosts: Host names the server answers to. Default: loopback and any *.ts.net. Tighter: your machine's exact name.

this_host._comment: This machine. id defaults to the hostname.
this_host._disks: Mount points. A LUKS or ZFS volume that is only mounted after unlocking shows as missing until then.

hosts._comment: With `tailscale up --accept-dns=false` this server can't resolve MagicDNS names: use the 100.x address. A name that doesn't resolve shows as a warning, not as asleep.
hosts.name: Gaming PC

checks.name: CouchDB
checks._comment: 401 is fine: CouchDB with require_valid_user answers /_up only to logged-in users, but it is up.

_actions: Off by default. To turn on: set pending_dir and actions. Your scripts write pending/*.json; the app's Approve button runs the command. Read the security notes first.
_chat: Off by default. chat_command gets the text on stdin and prints the answer.
